tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformance with the visual specification. The same STM section also carries a hygroscopicity procedure.

details.hygroscopicityProcedure: Weigh a glass weighing vessel with stopper (m1); add about 2 g of substance and weigh (m2); place the un-stoppered vessel in a climatic cabinet at 25 ± 1 °C for 24 h; stopper and weigh (m3); calculate the percentage increase in mass (expression not reproduced in the text). Very hygroscopic: increase >= 15 %; hygroscopic: 2 % to 15 %; slightly hygroscopic: < 2 %.

tests.procedure: Solubility by the BP stepwise method (100 mg in 0.1 mL, then +0.9 mL, +2 mL, +7 mL; then 10 mg / 1 mg in 10 mL), shaking 1 min then 15 min at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C at each step. Repeat with ethanol (96 per cent) and methylene chloride.

details.steps: 100 mg + 0.1 mL (very soluble); + 0.9 mL (freely soluble); + 2 mL (soluble); + 7 mL (sparingly soluble); 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble); 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble); else practically insoluble

tests.procedure: Dissolve 0.5 g in 50 mL water; immediately add 5 mL hydrochloric acid R1; filter; wash the precipitate with water; dry in vacuo at 80 °C for 2 h; determine the melting point with a calibrated melting point apparatus (BP Appendix V A).

details.reagent: Hydrochloric Acid R1: dilute 70 g of hydrochloric acid to 100 mL with water

tests.procedure: TLC on octadecylsilyl silica gel F254 plate. Test solution (a): 0.10 g in 10 mL water, immediately add 2 mL hydrochloric acid, shake with 50 mL 1,1-dimethylethyl methyl ether, evaporate the upper layer to dryness, take up residue in 10 mL acetone. Test solution (b): dilute 1 mL of (a) to 10 mL with acetone. Reference (a): 10 mg propyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS (or sodium propyl RS/WS) in acetone to 10 mL. Reference (b): 10 mg Ethyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS in 1 mL of test solution (a), dilute to 10 mL with acetone. Apply 5 µL of (b), ref (a), ref (b); develop over 2/3 of plate; dry in air; examine at 254 nm. System suitability: reference (b) shows 2 clearly separated principal spots.

details.plate: TLC octadecyl silyl silica gel F254
details.mobilePhase: glacial acetic acid : water : methanol (1:30:70 V/V/V)
details.systemSuitability: Reference solution (b): chromatogram shows 2 clearly separated principal spots
details.testSolutionA: 0.10 g in 10 mL water + 2 mL hydrochloric acid, shake with 50 mL 1,1-dimethylethyl methyl ether, evaporate upper layer, take up in 10 mL acetone
details.testSolutionB: 1 mL of (a) diluted to 10 mL with acetone
details.referenceA: 10 mg propyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS or WS (or sodium propyl RS or WS) in acetone, to 10 mL
details.referenceB: 10 mg Ethyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS in 1 mL of test solution (a), diluted to 10 mL with acetone

tests.procedure: To 1 mL of solution S add 1 mL water and 2 mL of 150 g/L potassium carbonate; heat to boiling (no precipitate); add 4 mL potassium pyroantimonate solution; heat to boiling; cool in iced water. Dense white precipitate expected.

details.reagent: Potassium Pyroantimonate Solution R1: 2.0 g potassium pyroantimonate in 95 mL hot water, cool quickly, add 2.5 g potassium hydroxide in 50 mL water and 1 mL dilute sodium hydroxide solution, stand 24 h, filter, dilute to 150 mL with water

tests.procedure: HPLC related substances. Test solution: 50.0 mg in 2.5 mL methanol, dilute to 50.0 mL with mobile phase, then 10.0 mL to 100.0 mL with mobile phase. Reference (a): 5 mg Ethyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS (impurity C), 5 mg 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (impurity A) and 5 mg of the substance in mobile phase to 100.0 mL, then 1.0 mL to 10.0 mL. Reference (b): 50.0 mg propyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS (or sodium propyl RS/WS) in 2.5 mL methanol, to 50.0 mL with mobile phase, then 10.0 mL to 100.0 mL. Reference (c): 1.0 mL of test solution to 20.0 mL with mobile phase, then 1.0 mL to 10.0 mL.

details.column: l = 0.15 m, 4.6 mm ID, end-capped octadecylsilyl silica gel for chromatography (ODS, 5 µm)
details.mobilePhase: 6.8 g/L potassium dihydrogen phosphate solution : methanol (35:65 V/V)
details.injected: test solution and reference solutions (a) and (c)
details.runTime: 2.5 times the retention time of propyl Para hydroxybenzoate
details.relativeRetention: vs propyl Para hydroxybenzoate (about 4.5 min): impurity A about 0.3, impurity C about 0.7
details.systemSuitability: Reference solution (a): resolution minimum 5.0 between the peaks of impurity C and propyl Para hydroxybenzoate
details.correctionFactor: multiply the peak area of impurity A by 1.4 for the calculation of content

stmLimits.impurityA: NMT 8 times the area of the principal peak of reference (c) (4.0 per cent)
stmLimits.eachUnspecified: NMT the area of the principal peak of reference (c) (0.5 per cent)
stmLimits.sumOtherThanA: NMT twice the area of the principal peak of reference (c) (1.0 per cent)
stmLimits.disregardLimit: 0.2 times the area of the principal peak of reference (c) (0.1 per cent)

reagents: Propyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS or WS

tests.procedure: Limit test. Sample: 10 mL of solution S + 30 mL water + 1 mL nitric acid, dilute to 50 mL with water, shake, filter; dilute 10 mL of filtrate to 15 mL with water, add 1 mL dilute nitric acid, pour as a single addition into a tube containing 1 mL silver nitrate solution R2. Standard: 14 mL chloride standard (5 ppm Cl) + 1 mL water + 1 mL dilute nitric acid, poured into 1 mL silver nitrate R2. Stand 5 min protected from light; view laterally against a black background; opalescence of test not more intense than standard.

details.chlorideStandard5ppm: dilute with water to 100 times its volume a solution containing sodium chloride equivalent to 0.824 g NaCl in 1000.0 mL (immediately before use)
details.silverNitrateR2: 1.7 g silver nitrate in water to 100 mL
details.dilutedNitricAcid: 20 g nitric acid to 100 mL with water

tests.procedure: Limit test as written in the STM: to 25 mL solution S add 5 mL distilled water and 10 mL hydrochloric acid, dilute to 50 mL, shake, filter; dilute 10 mL of filtrate to 15 mL (solution 1). Add 3 mL of 250 g/L barium chloride to 4.5 mL sulfate standard (10 ppm SO4) R1, shake, stand 1 min; to 2.5 mL of this suspension add 15 mL of solution 1 and 0.5 mL acetic acid (test). Standard: same suspension 2.5 mL + 15 mL sulfate standard (10 ppm SO4) + 0.5 mL acetic acid. After 5 min opalescence of test not more intense than standard.

details.sulfateStandard10ppm: dilute with distilled water to 100 times its volume a solution of dipotassium sulfate equivalent to 0.181 g K2SO4 in 100.0 mL (immediately before use)

tests.procedure: HPLC assay against propyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS or sodium propyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS. Test solution: 50.0 mg in 2.5 mL methanol, dilute to 50.0 mL with mobile phase, then 10.0 mL to 100.0 mL with mobile phase. Standard solution: 50.0 mg of the standard in 2.5 mL methanol, to 50.0 mL with mobile phase, then 10.0 mL to 100.0 mL. System suitability: 6 replicate injections of the standard solution.

details.column: l = 0.15 m, 4.6 mm ID, end-capped octadecylsilyl silica gel for chromatography (ODS, 5 µm)
details.mobilePhase: 6.8 g/L potassium dihydrogen phosphate solution : methanol (35:65 V/V)
details.systemSuitability: 6 replicate injections of the Standard solution (no numeric criterion stated)
details.finalDilution: 50.0 mL then 10.0 mL to 100.0 mL (mobile phase)
details.calculation: Assay % = (PAt / PAst) x (Act.Wt.std / Theo.Wt.std) x (Theo.Wt.test / Act.Wt.test) x (100 / (100 - MC)) x Potency; the text prints the factors as PAt/PAst, Act.Wt.std/Act.Wt.std, Theo.Wt.test/Theo.Wt.test, 100/(100-MC). PAt/PAst = mean peak area test/standard; MC = moisture content of working standard; Potency = assay of working standard. Calculate sodium propylparaben using the declared content of Sodium Propyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS; if Propyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS is used multiply by the correction factor 1.122.
details.limit: 94.0 per cent to 102.0 per cent (anhydrous substance)
